items.title: The recommended GitLab configuration for agentic engineering
items.summary: Agents keep getting better at more than drafting code. Teams already use them to move work through review, repair pipelines, and push changes toward merge. That speed only helps if every change is based on the software lifecycle context that lives in a unified platform and still passes the same gates your organization trusts. Without it, context, controls, and evidence fragment across people and tools into a shadow software factory.Identity, policy, CI pipelines, security, approvals, and audits have to travel with the change from plan through merge and into production. A local harness alone does not hold that full picture. Your coding harness and GitLab Duo Agent Platform are built to work in tandem, so coding agents can move quickly while GitLab certifies their work on the way to production.Software teams get to use different coding tools and agents they prefer, while their GitLab instance makes sure that every change is safe to ship. GitLab stays cloud-neutral, model-neutral, and agent-neutral, so you keep the harnesses, models, and deployment path that fit your organization.Let us show you how to configure your agentic engineering environment to drive greater automation throughout your workflow. You stay in the harness you already use and connect to GitLab Duo Agent Platform once with a skill. Longer, repository-aware workflows run on GitLab, and every merge request still hits the same reviews, pipelines, scans, and approval policies.In this article, we will focus on Claude Code as the local harness because that’s what we see most of our customers using but this same flow can apply to the local harness of your choosing, including Duo CLI.How to configure your agentic engineering environmentIf you already do most of your coding in a local harness, keep working there and wire it to GitLab Duo Agent Platform. From the terminal, you can direct lifecycle work to agentic workflows that run inside GitLab:Picking up an issue and opening a merge requestReviewing every MR as it landsResolving merge conflictsRepairing a pipeline that just failedWith GitLab Ultimate, triaging and fixing security findings once code landsClaude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, and others become the place from where you direct that work.Part 1 is the setup:Install the GitLab Duo setup skill, ask Claude Code to run it, and it sets up your whole top-level group with the necessary settings, the flows, an automation in every project, and the MCP connection.Part 2 walks through four workflows:You can try them as soon as the setup is done, each driven from Claude Code:Find an issue assigned to you and hand it to the Developer flow.Get automated code reviews on your merge requests, act on the findings without leaving your harness, and resolve any conflicts that pop up.Use an automation to fix a failed pipeline.On Ultimate, triage and fix security findings with the security flows.When you want an even tighter loop:The MR followup skill guides your local harness through the steps above even faster. The skill helps local agents monitor progress on the repo-side and take actions on your behalf to speed things along.What you get from the combined path:Move faster: Automatic review, pipeline repair, and (on Ultimate) security triage keep changes moving without leaving your harness.Build trust: The same engineering and security standards apply to every MR, with oversight and an audit trail in GitLab.Reduce complexity: Automate the handoff between your harness and GitLab so lifecycle work shares one context, one set of gates, and one audit trail.What you need before you start:A GitLab.com top-level group with GitLab Credits (Premium and Ultimate groups get access to promotional free credits each month for each user). The security workflow in Use Case 4 requires Ultimate licensing for your GitLab instance.A project in that group with a pipeline, a few open issues, and an open merge request or two, so the workflows have something to act on.The Owner role on the top-level group, so the skill can set up the whole group. If you're a Maintainer on the project but not a group owner, the skill sets up just that project and lists what to ask your Owner.Claude Code installed and signed in, plus git and the GitLab CLI (glab, signed in with glab auth login ), which the skill uses to read and change settings.Part 1: Guided setup with a skillThe GitLab Duo setup skill accelerates the connection from inside your harness. You install the skill once, ask Claude Code to set up GitLab Duo. The skill sets up your group as it turns on group-wide Duo Agent Platform workflows, creates the Fix CI/CD Pipeline automation where needed, connects to GitLab MCP server, and reports anything left for you to finish.Install the skillgit clone https://gitlab.com/gitlab-da/projects/agentic-eng-config.gitcp -R agentic-eng-config/skills/gitlab-duo-setup ~/.claude/skills/cp -R agentic-eng-config/skills/gitlab-mr-followup ~/.claude/skills/Then Claude Code picks it up in the running session.
